claims: Valentina Tereshkova became the first woman in space on June 16, 1963, aboard the Vostok 6 mission.
Valentina Tereshkova was a former textile worker.
Valentina Tereshkova completed 48 orbits around Earth.
Valentina Tereshkova's space mission lasted just under 71 hours.
Valentina Tereshkova remains the only woman to have flown a solo space mission.
Valentina Tereshkova's flight lasted 70 hours and 50 minutes.
Valentina Tereshkova's flight orbited the Earth 48 times.
Valentina Tereshkova was chosen from over 400 applicants.
Valentina Tereshkova was chosen due to her expertise in parachuting.
Cosmonauts had to eject and parachute from their capsules upon return.
Valentina Tereshkova's Wikipedia biography and Britannica entry detail that she became a major general in the Soviet Air Force.
Valentina Tereshkova's Wikipedia biography and Britannica entry detail that she became a prominent politician.
The European Space Agency notes Valentina Tereshkova was born in 1937 in central Russia.
The European Space Agency notes Valentina Tereshkova was selected for the cosmonaut corps in 1962.
Valentina Tereshkova was the first woman in space two years after Yuri Gagarin
